accepted.s: The Department of Space functions directly under the:
o: Union Minister of Science and Technology
accepted.x: The Department of Space works directly under the Prime Minister.
accepted.tq: Authority-identification question using nearby constitutional and executive offices as distractors.
accepted.sec: ISRO formation - year, Department of Space and Space Commission

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
accepted.x: IN-SPACe was established in 2020. Antrix was established in 1992 and NSIL in 2019.
accepted.tq: Match each commercial space arm with its establishment year.
accepted.sec: ISRO formation - year, Department of Space and Space Commission

accepted.s:
With reference to the commercial arms and regulatory institution associated with the Indian space sector, consider the following statements:
1. Antrix was established in 1992.
2. Antrix received Miniratna status in 2008.
3. NSIL was established in 2019.
4. IN-SPACe was established in 2020 and has its headquarters at Ahmedabad.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements are correct. Antrix dates from 1992 and received Miniratna status in 2008; NSIL was established in 2019, and IN-SPACe in 2020 with headquarters at Ahmedabad.
accepted.tq: Statement-combination question testing dates, status and location together.
accepted.sec: ISRO formation - year, Department of Space and Space Commission

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly represents the targets of the Indian Space Vision 2047?
o: Bharatiya Antariksh Station by 2040 and an Indian on the Moon by 2035
Bharatiya Antariksh Station by 2047 and an Indian on the Moon by 2040
Bharatiya Antariksh Station by 2030 and an Indian on the Moon by 2035
Bharatiya Antariksh Station by 2035 and an Indian on the Moon by 2040
accepted.x: The vision envisages the Bharatiya Antariksh Station by 2035 and placing an Indian on the Moon by 2040.
accepted.tq: Close-year discrimination between two linked national targets.
accepted.sec: Indian Space Vision 2047 - space station, crewed lunar landing, next missions

accepted.s: Gaganyaan is planned to carry:
o: Four crew members to a 400-km orbit for seven days
Three crew members to the Moon for three days
Three crew members to a 400-km orbit for three days
Two astronauts to a geostationary orbit for seven days
accepted.x: Gaganyaan is planned to carry a crew of three to an orbit approximately 400 km above Earth for three days, followed by splashdown in Indian waters.
accepted.tq: Numerical recall of crew size, orbital altitude and mission duration.
accepted.sec: Indian Space Vision 2047 - space station, crewed lunar landing, next missions

accepted.s: The planned recovery mode of the Gaganyaan crew module is:
o: Landing on a prepared runway in Sriharikota
Parachute landing in the Thar Desert
accepted.x: The Gaganyaan crew module is planned to splash down in Indian waters.
accepted.tq: Scenario-based identification of the mission’s planned recovery method.
accepted.sec: Indian Space Vision 2047 - space station, crewed lunar landing, next missions

accepted.s: SOLVE, associated with the Gaganyaan programme, is intended to:
o: Dock two satellites in lunar orbit
Test crew-module recovery using a sub-orbital vehicle
Deploy a space telescope into geostationary orbit
accepted.x: SOLVE is a sub-orbital vehicle intended to test crew-module recovery.
accepted.tq: Function-based identification of a named technology demonstrator.
accepted.sec: Indian Space Vision 2047 - space station, crewed lunar landing, next missions

accepted.s:
Which of the following missions are identified as planned or forthcoming missions in the Indian Space Vision 2047 roadmap?
1. Chandrayaan-4
2. Chandrayaan-5
3. Venus Orbiter Mission
4. NISAR
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Chandrayaan-4, Chandrayaan-5 and the Venus Orbiter Mission are identified as next missions in the roadmap. NISAR is an Indo-US mission launched in 2025, not part of this listed next-mission group.
accepted.tq: Separate future roadmap missions from an already completed international mission.
accepted.sec: Indian Space Vision 2047 - space station, crewed lunar landing, next missions

accepted.s: The approved cost of the Venus Orbiter Mission is:
accepted.x: The approved Venus Orbiter Mission has a cost of Rs 1,236 crore.
accepted.tq: Exact-figure recall with digit-transposition distractors.
accepted.sec: Indian Space Vision 2047 - space station, crewed lunar landing, next missions

accepted.s: Which one of the following combinations correctly represents the stated targets for the Indian space sector?
o: 44 launches a year, a 50-billion-dollar space economy and more than 300 space start-ups
50 launches a year, a 44-billion-dollar space economy and more than 440 space start-ups
40 launches a year, a 44-billion-dollar space economy and more than 400 space start-ups
50 launches a year, a 440-billion-dollar space economy and more than 44 space start-ups
accepted.x: The stated targets are 50 launches annually, a 44-billion-dollar space economy and more than 440 space start-ups.
accepted.tq: Keep the three quantitative targets together and avoid swapping their units.
accepted.sec: Indian Space Vision 2047 - space station, crewed lunar landing, next missions

accepted.s: The new launch pad mentioned for the Indian space programme is being established at:
accepted.x: A new launch pad is planned at Kulasekarapattinam.
accepted.tq: Direct location recall using other space-sector locations as distractors.
accepted.sec: Indian Space Vision 2047 - space station, crewed lunar landing, next missions

accepted.s: Rakesh Sharma became the first Indian in space aboard:
accepted.x: Rakesh Sharma was the first Indian in space and flew aboard Soyuz T-11 in April 1984, under the USSR programme.
accepted.tq: Combine the person, spacecraft and date while rejecting one-element swaps.
accepted.sec: International cooperation milestones - Soyuz T-11, Indo-French and Indo-US

accepted.s: Shubhanshu Shukla was associated with which of the following achievements?
o: Leading the first Indian crewed lunar landing in 2040
Launching NISAR on an Ariane-1 rocket in 2013
Flying to the International Space Station on Axiom-4 in June-July 2025
Becoming the first Indian in space on Soyuz T-11 in 1984
accepted.x: Shubhanshu Shukla flew to the International Space Station on Axiom-4 during June-July 2025.
accepted.tq: Person-event discrimination against nearby Indian space milestones.
accepted.sec: International cooperation milestones - Soyuz T-11, Indo-French and Indo-US

accepted.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. SITE — NASA cooperation
2. NISAR — NASA-ISRO SAR
3. APPLE — Ariane-1
4. SARAL — 2013
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
accepted.x: All four pairs are correctly matched. SITE involved NASA cooperation in 1975-76; NISAR is NASA-ISRO SAR; APPLE flew on Ariane-1; and SARAL dates to 2013.
accepted.tq: Use sure pairings between mission names, agencies, launch vehicles and years.
accepted.sec: International cooperation milestones - Soyuz T-11, Indo-French and Indo-US

accepted.s: The Satellite Instructional Television Experiment (SITE), conducted in cooperation with NASA, belongs to which period?
accepted.x: SITE was conducted with NASA cooperation during 1975-76.
accepted.tq: Period recall with decade-based distractors.
accepted.sec: International cooperation milestones - Soyuz T-11, Indo-French and Indo-US

accepted.s: Which of the following statements regarding Indo-French space cooperation is correct?
o: APPLE was launched on Ariane-1, while Megha-Tropiques and SARAL were associated with the cooperation.
APPLE was launched on Soyuz T-11, while Megha-Tropiques was an Indo-US mission.
SARAL was launched before APPLE and was associated exclusively with NASA.
Megha-Tropiques and SARAL were Indian military satellites launched from Sriharikota.
accepted.x: APPLE was launched on Ariane-1, and Megha-Tropiques and SARAL are listed as Indo-French cooperation milestones.
accepted.tq: Reject swapped partners and incorrect launch-vehicle associations.
accepted.sec: International cooperation milestones - Soyuz T-11, Indo-French and Indo-US

accepted.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with Indo-US space cooperation?
accepted.x: NISAR, meaning NASA-ISRO SAR, was launched in 2025. APPLE, SARAL and SITE belong to different pairings or cooperation milestones.
accepted.tq: Find the correctly matched cooperation pair among deliberately swapped associations.
accepted.sec: International cooperation milestones - Soyuz T-11, Indo-French and Indo-US

accepted.s: The Technical Implementing Plan prepared by ISRO and ESA relates to:
o: Recovery testing of the SOLVE vehicle
Construction of the Bharatiya Antariksh Station
accepted.x: The ISRO-ESA Technical Implementing Plan concerns ground-tracking support for Gaganyaan. The two agencies have also held talks on Venus missions.
accepted.tq: Identify the specific institutional purpose rather than the broader cooperation theme.
accepted.sec: International cooperation milestones - Soyuz T-11, Indo-French and Indo-US

accepted.s: Which of the following statements best reflects the stated position regarding ISRO’s role after privatisation of the space sector?
o: Its role is by no means diminishing.
Its role has been completely transferred to private companies.
Its role has ended with the creation of IN-SPACe.
Its role is restricted exclusively to launching foreign satellites.
accepted.x: IN-SPACe chairman Pawan Kumar Goenka stated that ISRO’s role is “by no means diminishing” after privatisation.
accepted.tq: Test the exact official position while using extreme-word distractors.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. India has 56 active space assets.
2. Foreign direct investment up to 100% is permitted in non-sensitive space segments.
3. More than 400 foreign satellites have been launched on Indian rockets.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct: India has 56 active space assets, permits up to 100% FDI in non-sensitive segments, and has launched more than 400 foreign satellites on Indian rockets.
accepted.tq: Combine current quantitative indicators and select the all-correct code.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Sriharikota — all orbital launches from India
accepted.x: SpaDeX is associated with India’s first docking achievement, not the first Indian satellite. Aryabhata was the first Indian satellite.
accepted.tq: Use the first/last list to identify the swapped achievement.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s:
Arrange the following milestones in chronological order:
A. SITE with NASA
B. Rakesh Sharma’s Soyuz T-11 flight
C. Formation of ISRO
D. Launch of NISAR
accepted.x: ISRO was formed in 1969, SITE occurred in 1975-76, Rakesh Sharma flew in 1984, and NISAR was launched in 2025.
accepted.tq: Fix the earliest and latest milestones first, then place the middle events by year.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly represents the firsts associated with the Indian space programme?
o: Rohini—first satellite; Aryabhata—first indigenous launch; SARAL—first geostationary satellite; NISAR—first docking
NISAR—first satellite; APPLE—first indigenous launch; Aryabhata—first geostationary satellite; Rohini—first docking
Aryabhata—first satellite; Rohini—first indigenous launch; APPLE—first geostationary satellite; SpaDeX—first docking
APPLE—first satellite; Aryabhata—first docking; Rohini—first geostationary satellite; SpaDeX—first indigenous launch
accepted.x: The listed firsts are Aryabhata as the first satellite, Rohini as the first indigenous launch, APPLE as the first geostationary satellite and SpaDeX as the first docking achievement.
accepted.tq: Match each milestone with its unique distinction and avoid swapping the firsts.
